Nigerian Exchange Group Plc has acquired a 10 per cent equity stake in the Nairobi Securities Exchange, a strategic investment that extends the Group’s participation in East Africa and advances its pan-African growth strategy. According to a statement issued by the Group, the move aligns with its priority of building regional leadership through partnerships and African market integration, while strengthening its investment presence across West and East Africa. The latest development builds on NGX Group’s earlier strategic investment in the Ethiopian Securities Exchange, further demonstrating the company’s long-term commitment to participating in the development and growth of African capital market infrastructure. The acquisition provides NGX Group with exposure to one of East Africa’s most established capital markets, broadening its investment portfolio beyond Nigeria and positioning it to benefit from the long-term growth of the region’s capital markets and increasing financial integration across the continent. The Group noted that the transaction reflects a disciplined approach to capital allocation, balancing strategic growth opportunities with its commitment to sustainable shareholder returns. Capital market stakeholders seek unified digital platforms, reforms Inflation drops to 14.05% – NBS report NGX Group acquires 10% stake in Nairobi securities exchange Commenting on the investment, the Group Chairman, NGX Group, Alhaji Umaru Kwairanga, said, “African capital markets are at an inflection point, where integration is moving from aspiration to architecture. Exchange groups that commit patient capital to market infrastructure will help shape how capital flows across the continent. Our investment in the Nairobi Securities Exchange is a disciplined, long-term step in that direction, strengthening the financial linkages between West and East Africa while creating opportunities for sustainable shareholder value.” Also speaking, the Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, NGX Group, Temi Popoola, explained that the acquisition underscores the Group’s drive to build a more diversified and resilient exchange with a stronger continental footprint. He said, “This investment reflects our strategy to build a more diversified and resilient exchange group with a stronger presence across African markets. Kenya is a cornerstone of East Africa’s financial ecosystem, and our investment in NSE provides exposure to its long-term growth potential while broadening our sources of investment returns beyond Nigeria. “Both markets have already shown what closer collaboration can achieve for issuers and investors, and a shareholding relationship gives that collaboration permanence. We remain focused on disciplined capital allocation and investments that deliver sustainable value to our shareholders over the long term.” Through these cross-border investments, NGX Group stated that it would continue to pursue opportunities that enhance its regional participation, diversify its sources of investment returns, and support the development of more connected and competitive African capital markets. Nigerian Exchange Group Plc operates as an integrated market infrastructure group with interests across Nigeria’s capital market ecosystem, supporting capital formation, investment access, market development, and the provision of financial market infrastructure through its subsidiaries and strategic investments.
